claims.claim: UGIES outperforms state-of-the-art dataset pruning methods on CIFAR-10/100 with ResNet-18 (Table 1).
claims.evidence: The logbook explicitly states it does not present paper-reported benchmark values as reproduced measurements, and no CIFAR-10/100 experiments with ResNet-18 were executed.

claims.claim: On ImageNet-1K, UGIES achieves lossless or better-than-lossless pruning with ResNet-50 and Swin-T at moderate pruning ratios (Table 2).
claims.evidence: No ImageNet-1K experiments with ResNet-50 or Swin-T were run; the logbook only performs formal mathematical analysis and does not address empirical benchmark performance.

claims.claim: With ResNet-50 on ImageNet-1K at a 50% pruning ratio, UGIES reaches the same accuracy while saving 43.2% total training cost (Table 3).
claims.evidence: No training-cost or accuracy experiments on ImageNet-1K at 50% pruning ratio were conducted; the logbook is limited to formal verification of the mathematical claims.

claims.claim: Ablations show combining intrinsic and extrinsic importance terms outperforms using either component alone across pruning ratios (Table 4).
claims.evidence: No ablation experiments comparing intrinsic-only, extrinsic-only, and combined importance terms were executed; the logbook does not address this empirical claim.

raw_verdict.overall: The logbook provides rigorous exact-arithmetic formal evidence that falsifies the MWCP formulation's objective equivalence (Claim 1) and the submodularity/greedy-guarantee argument (Claim 2), citing specific witnesses such as a marginal sequence of 1/1 then 3/1 that violates diminishing returns. However, all four empirical benchmark claims (Claims 3–6) are entirely unaddressed because no training experiments were conducted.
